title: India and Poland Set 2030 Trade Goal, Deepen Defence and Space Ties
excerpt: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk agreed in New Delhi on Thursday to double bilateral trade by 2030, press for early implementation of the India-EU free trade agreement, and expand co-development in defence, space and energy.
body:
• India and Poland agreed on Thursday to double bilateral trade by 2030, according to the joint statement issued after talks in New Delhi.
  • Modi invited Polish companies to co-develop and co-produce with India in defence, space and energy, and announced an India-Poland Startup Bridge.
  • Both leaders pressed for prompt signing, ratification and implementation of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement.
  • The joint statement condemned terrorism, backed action against UNSC 1267-listed entities, and recorded Polish support for India's UNSC candidature for 2028-29.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk agreed on Thursday, October 22, to double bilateral trade between India and Poland by 2030, according to a joint statement issued after their meeting at Hyderabad House in New Delhi. The leaders pressed for the prompt signing and ratification of the EU-India Free Trade Agreement and its timely implementation, to unlock opportunities for commerce and investment, diversify value chains and open new markets, the statement said, as reported by ANI via LatestLY.

Tusk is on an official visit to India from October 21 to 23, the first visit by a Polish prime minister to India since 2010, according to ANI reporting carried by Devdiscourse. He arrived in New Delhi on Wednesday at Modi's invitation, accompanied by Poland's Minister of Finance and Economy Andrzej Domanski and a business delegation, and paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat on Thursday. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar also called on Tusk during the day.

Context & Background

India and Poland elevated their relationship to a Strategic Partnership during Modi's visit to Poland in August 2024. Thursday's talks built on that framework, covering AI, green technologies, critical minerals and defence, as well as trade, investment, education, culture and people-to-people exchanges, the Ministry of External Affairs said. Modi pointed to the economic momentum on both sides, noting that Poland's GDP had crossed USD 1 trillion and that India had registered growth of 7.8 per cent in the last quarter.

"Today we agreed to deepen our ties in the fields of defence, space and energy. In all these strategic sectors, we invite Polish companies to engage in co-development and co-production with India."

On strategic sectors, Modi said the two sides would forge new partnerships using Polish expertise in critical minerals and coal gasification. The joint statement identified space cooperation as a key element of the partnership, promoted stronger institutional and industry-level engagement, and noted that an MoU on critical minerals is under negotiation. The leaders also agreed to collaborative research on AI, semiconductors and quantum technologies, welcomed cooperation on battery recycling and rare earth refining, and announced an India-Poland Startup Bridge and technology hackathons for young people in both countries.

Impact/Analysis

The trade push rests heavily on the India-EU agreement. Modi said its implementation would open opportunities for Indian exports of machinery, chemicals, plastics and engineering goods to Poland, while advanced manufacturing, food processing, biotechnology, railways and mobility could attract Polish investment. Tusk expressed appreciation for Indian investments in Poland and described Poland as a gateway for Indian firms seeking to expand across Central and Eastern Europe and the wider European market, according to the joint statement. Both leaders welcomed the India-Poland Business Forum held during the visit and urged companies to partner in industrial machinery, defence, infrastructure, pharmaceuticals, mining and critical minerals, energy and ICT.

The joint statement also carried strong language on security, as reported by Nation Press. The two leaders condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all forms, condemned the terrorist attack in Pahalgam on April 22, 2025 in the strongest terms, called for action against terrorists and entities designated by the UNSC 1267 sanctions committee, backed early adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism, and agreed to establish a dedicated counter-terrorism dialogue. Poland expressed support for India's membership of a reformed and expanded UN Security Council and reiterated support for India's candidature for a non-permanent seat for 2028-29. On Ukraine, both leaders expressed deepest concern over the war and its impact on global food and energy security, and called for a comprehensive, just and lasting peace consistent with the UN Charter.

What's Next

Tusk is scheduled to travel to Bengaluru on October 23 to engage with leaders from India's information technology and space sectors, after participating in the India-Poland Business Forum in New Delhi. The joint statement pointed to specific follow-through: direct talks between civil aviation authorities on direct flights linking Poland and India, resumed work by the bilateral working group on agriculture, and cooperation between ports, including through the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor initiative. Whether the 2030 trade target is met will depend on the EU-India FTA entering into force and on the business partnerships the two governments urged companies to build during this visit.
